::: {.spotlight}
### Carceral Ecologies
[Partner: UCLA Institute for Society and Genetics (Nicholas Shapiro)]{.partners}

DSC and DataSquad provided multi-year research support, including R server
infrastructure, data processing, and training, for work on a massive helicopter
surveillance dataset that outstripped the lab's ability to host locally. DataSquad
members Lawrence Lee and Madeline Kim built the R-based solution behind the speedup
below. Kate McInerny, a student on the project, first encountered DSC through
Professor Kelly Lytle Hernández's African American 188 course, was hired into the
Carceral Ecologies lab, and kept building her data skills through DSC workshops
before graduating to Sciences Po. That work became the pilot study behind a $5
million grant that established the Dana Center for Neuroscience and Society.

> *"This work wouldn't have happened without your team!"*
> — Dr. Nicholas Shapiro, UCLA Institute for Society and Genetics

[**Outcome:** processing time cut from ~318 minutes to ~2 minutes (~159x faster). **Impact:** coverage in the *Los Angeles Times*, *The New Yorker*, and *Bloomberg*.]{.impact}
:::

::: {.spotlight}
### BioCritical Studies Lab
[Partner: UCLA (Grace Sosa; Terence Keel)]{.partners}

A multi-year collaboration (2021 to 2024) on data integration, statistical analysis,
and visualization for a comprehensive U.S. deaths-in-custody dataset, with tools built
for the lab to maintain independently. DataSquad cleaned redundant and non-critical
data points, reducing the dataset from 41,466 to 29,208 records (~30% smaller) while
preserving analytical value, then built visualizations and tools to maintain and
update it going forward. The dataset has supported projects funded by NIH, NSF, and
the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation. Prof. Keel became one of six recipients of UCLA's
2024 Public Impact Research Awards, and DSC's work is featured in his book, *The
Coroner's Silence: Death Records and the Hidden Victims of Police Violence*.

> *"It is one of the most impactful resources I have engaged with [...] at UCLA."*
> — Grace Sosa, Assistant Director, BioCritical Studies Lab

[**Impact:** supported research recognized through UCLA's 2024 Public Impact Research Awards, contributing to public-facing scholarship and teaching.]{.impact}
:::

::: {.spotlight}
### Refugee Material Culture Initiative
[Partner: Professor Kelly Nguyen]{.partners}

DSC's 3D and emerging-technology work, led by Doug Daniels with DataSquad members
Bianca Badajos and Connor Lim, processed multiple artifacts from Vietnamese refugees
in collaboration with the Vietnamese Heritage Museum. The team helped curate multiple
digital exhibits, including a 7-day narrative documenting a refugee family's maritime
escape across the Pacific Ocean, built from 3D scans of the boat and related objects.

[**Outcome:** digital exhibits built from 3D-scanned historical artifacts, made freely public. **Impact:** advances faculty research using state-of-the-art documentation and preservation of cultural heritage.]{.impact}
:::
